Here’s a quick rundown of the most common flight‑booking tools, APIs, and platforms you can tap into—whether you’re building a travel app, automating searches, or just looking for the best way to pull flight data:

| Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use case | Notes |
|----------------|----------------|-----------------|-------|
| **Skyscanner API** (RapidAPI) | Search flights, hotels, car rentals; price alerts | Build a multi‑service travel search engine | Free tier limits ~200 requests/day; paid plans unlock higher limits & more features |
| **Google Flights API** (via Google Cloud) | Flight availability & pricing (limited public access) | Integrate Google’s flight search UI or data into your own site | Requires OAuth & usage quotas; not fully open to all developers |
| **Amadeus for Developers** | Flights, hotels, airport info, travel intelligence | Enterprise‑grade travel solutions | Offers “Flights Live Availability” & “Flight Offers Search”; free tier ~1000 calls/month |
| **Travelport Universal API** | Global distribution system (GDS) access – bookings, inventory, fares | Large travel agencies, corporate booking portals | Requires partnership & licensing; high cost but full GDS coverage |
| **Sabre API** | GDS access, flight search, booking, fare rules | Corporate travel, airline partners | Similar to Travelport – enterprise‑level, requires partnership |
| **Expedia Affiliate Network** | Hotel & flight search, booking, commissions | Affiliate sites, travel blogs | Pay‑per‑click or pay‑per‑booking models |
| **Priceline Partner Network** | Hotel & flight search, booking | Affiliate marketing, travel comparison sites | Commission‑based; requires approval |
| **CheapOair API** | Flight search & booking | Budget travel sites, coupon aggregators | Commission‑based; easy integration |
| **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status, historical data | Tracking apps, aviation analytics | Paid tiers start at ~$50/month |
| **OpenSky Network API** | ADS‑B data, real‑time aircraft positions | Aviation enthusiasts, research | Free for non‑commercial use; rate‑limited |
| **AviationStack API** | Flight status, schedules, airports, airlines | Data feeds for travel apps | Free tier ~5000 calls/month; paid plans for higher volume |
| **Skiplagged API** (via RapidAPI) | Hidden‑city ticketing data, price comparisons | Price‑comparison engines, fare‑alert bots | Free tier limited; paid plans unlock bulk queries |
| **Kayak API** (via RapidAPI) | Flights, hotels, car rentals | Aggregator sites, price‑comparison widgets | Free tier ~200 calls/day; paid plans for higher limits |
| **Rome2rio API** (via RapidAPI) | Multi‑modal journey planner (flights + trains, buses, ferries) | Trip planning apps | Free tier ~200 calls/day; paid plans for higher volume |

### How to choose:
1. **Volume & Scale** – If you expect millions of queries, look at enterprise GDS APIs (Travelport, Sabre).  
2. **Cost vs. Features** – Free tiers are great for prototyping, but paid plans often unlock higher limits, richer data (e.g., fare rules, seat maps).  
3. **Data Freshness** – For real‑time tracking, use FlightAware or OpenSky.  
4. **Ease of Integration** – RapidAPI hubs (Skyscanner, Kayak, Skiplagged) simplify authentication and rate‑limit handling.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any specific API (pricing, SDKs, sample code, etc.)!
